The building is situated on the property line, within the current code-required setbacks, and predates modern zoning and building code standards. The garage is in an advanced state of disrepair and poses a potential safety hazard. It exhibits significant structural deterioration, including: • Extensive dry rot in framing members and wall sheathing • A compromised roof structure that is sagging and unstable • Active termite or pest damage • No longer structurally sound and at imminent risk of collapse Due to the degree of degradation, the structure is considered beyond reasonable repair or mitigation. The cost of rehabilitation far exceeds the value of the structure, and its location within current setbacks makes reconstruction in the same location non-compliant with existing County codes. There is no intention to rebuild or replace the garage at this time. The proposed demolition will improve safety on the property, eliminate blight, and allow for better long-term site management and use. All demolition activities will comply with applicable Sonoma County environmental and safety regulations, including: • Proper waste disposal and material recycling • Dust and debris control measures during demolition • Compliance with erosion and sediment control if required • Disconnection and capping of any utilities serving the structure • We respectfully request approval of this demolition based on the urgent need to remove a hazardous, non-code-conforming structure that is no longer viable. This action is in the best interest of public safety and the long-term stewardship of the property.

description: **RENEW PC EXPIRED** GRD20-0287 Pending completion of drainage and grading permit. GRD20-0287 - BRIAN KEEFER 6 MONTHS FROM 11/1/2024 RENEW grd20-0287 I am proposing to build a 3,000 square foot metal storage building with a 35 panel solar array on the roof. The proposed building will be in an area of my lot that is flat, and currently drains to the existing V-ditch at the south side property line. We have excavated an area of approximately 4,200 square feet (60' x 70'), and removed the existing Black Adobe soil to a depth of 36". We then installed structural fill compacted in 8" to 12" lifts. Currently, the elevation is exactly at the point it was prior to starting the work. The next phase will consist of an additional 12" of compacted structural fill, and then 6" of base rock under a 4"-5" concrete slab. The building foot print will be 60' wide (east to west) and 50' deep (north to south). I am proposing to slope away from all four sides of building pad and conform to existing grade. I am also proposing as part of this project to extend the existing driveway on the west side of property to the new proposed Metal building. This will require removing existing expansive soils and importing structural fill to build a base for the driveway.

The project is being constructed by the Gold Ridge Resources Conservation District with funding from Caltrans in cooperation with the landowners. Improvements will support mitigation work for the new Scotty Creek bridge mandated by the Coastal Commission. The water tank and some distribution improvements will be constructed within a conservation easement established for the purpose of implementing mitigation projects.

description: Owner is performing work along the shoreline of Russian River to resolve a violation. The violation resulted from hand-work Owner implemented to replace a deteriorating wood stairway and boatramp with a stairway and ramp consconstructed from metal gabion baskets filled with natural river cobbles from the river bed. Owner obtained CDFW and RWQCB permits to remove the gabion baskets, restore the pre-existing channel bank slope, and install new replacement stairway and ramp structures. The replacement structures are single piece pre-fabricated aluminum stairway and ramp (2 pieces) that will be fastened to new steel pipe piles driven into the ground and extending above finished grade 6-9". The owner obtained a geotechnical investigation report and geotechnical-structural design recommendations from Miller-Pacific Engineering group including pipe pile anchoring construction details and hardware details for fastening the pre-fab pieces to the pipe pile caps. The work will be performed by hand with hand tools carried to the work location on foot. There is no construction access for equipment. There is no excavation or stockpiling or production of exposed soil, etc. The Owner appplied for a Zoning Permit and a Grading Permit. All permit issuance is pending approval of a Building Permit.

description: Drill a replacement well, Class 1 with 5" PVC casing & 50' annular seal. Once new well has been constructed and activated destroy the existing well. Destruct method: Remove the pump equipment from the well and cut the steel casing off approximately 3' below grade. Fill the 6" steel casing with 3/8" pea gravel from the bottom at approximately 91' below grade to 33' below grade and use a mechanical Mills Knife perforating tool to perforate the steel casing from 33' to 3' below grade. A neat cement slurry is to be pumped into the well via a tremie pipe to seal the well from 33' below grade to just over the top of the steel casing approximately 3' below grade. Native soil is to be used to backfill the remaining hole to final grade.

description: The proposed project consists of embankment repairs at at three identified bank failure locations along a streamside easement road that travels alongside Sheephouse Creek through the Keller property. The road provides primary year- round access to the Riciloi residence, and the Project is designed to enhance riparian habitat, reduce future sediment delivery, and restore and protect the structural integrity of stream banks where the unpaved access road is vulnerable to collapse along the left bank of Sheephouse Creek. The project proposes boulder-ballasted wood structures (logs and logs with rootwads) that will act as bank-stabilization, energy dissipation, and in-stream habitat features. This design will meet project objectives by improving shallow water habitat and increasing the availability of velocity refugia for aquatic organisms, stabilizing streambanks and preventing large loads of fine sediment from polluting the stream system, preserving the natural aesthetic and restoring important fluvial geomorphic processes of Sheephouse Creek, as well as protecting and rebuilding portions of the easement road using a “no net fill” approach to avoid increasing flood risk.

description: AllStarz Pumping & Engineering will be performing the decommissioning and proper abandonment of the existing septic system located at the above- referenced property. The following scope outlines the full procedure we will undertake to comply with county and environmental regulations: 1. Expose Existing Septic Tanks Our crew will excavate and fully expose all existing septic tanks on site using appropriate equipment. All necessary precautions will be taken to avoid disturbing any nearby utilities, structures, or vegetation. 2. Pumping and Cleaning (if necessary) If any sewage, sludge, or liquid remains in the tanks, we will arrange for a licensed septic pumper to remove and legally dispose of the contents at an approved facility. 3. Perforation of Tank Bottoms After the tanks are emptied, we will puncture holes in the bottom of each tank to ensure proper drainage and prevent future water accumulation. 4. Collapse of Tanks The tanks will then be crushed and collapsed in place to reduce the potential for future ground settling or void formation. 5. Fill With Clean Crushed Rock The interior of each collapsed tank will be filled with clean, drainable crushed rock to stabilize the structure and maintain subsurface drainage. 6. Backfill and Compaction The excavation area will then be backfilled with a mixture of compacted gravel and clean native soil (or imported fill, if needed). Material will be placed and compacted in lifts to minimize future settling. 7. Final Grading The area will be finish-graded to restore natural contours and to promote positive surface drainage away from all structures.

description: Permit for a well destruct for old well. DATE: 6/10/2025 ESTIMATE SUBMITTED TO: Donald & Carole Mclain PO BOX 1263 707-938-2154 Sonoma, CA 95476 djmclain@pacbell.net JOB LOCATION: 1265 Oak Creek Dr, Sonoma, CA 05476 WE HEREBY SUBMIT SPECIFICATIONS AND ESTIMATES FOR: Proposal For Domestic Well Destruction. First Arolo Pump & Well will file for a Well Destruction Permit with Sonoma County Environmental Health department. Once permit is approved, Arolo will schedule to perform Well Destruct. Arolo will perform well destruction per plan approved process as per permit. Arolo will start by pulling existing well pump, drop pipe, wire, couplings and check valves out of old well. Load into trailer. Dig around existing well casing down 5’ from grade. Demo concrete seal. Cut steel casing down 4’ leaving 1’ of steel casing. Arolo will set up Rig and knife perforating/ripping tool. Send tool down on galv pipe. Rip casing from 30’ to top of casing at 4’ under grade. Pull galv pipe and tooling out of existing casing. Send 6yard of pea gravel down well and fill old casing from bottom to 40 below grade stopping the gravel. Set up Pour concrete down till well casing is filled up to top of casing and mushroom over. Arolo will call for inspection and clean-up site. Back fill hole around casing and level off. Arolo will provide proper paper work and documents for project. The well destruction will be documented in a short letter report to the NCRWCB and Sonoma County Environmental Health, and a California Department of Water Resources (DWR) Well Completion Report will be prepared and submitted to the DWR and Sonoma County.

description: I am applying for a no plan check construction permit in order to make repairs to the upper lateral of my sewer line. I have already applied for a sewer permit which relates to the repairs downstream of the sewer cleanout. I have been informed that I also need to apply for a construction permit for the repairs upstream of the sewer cleanout going into my home. In essence I am replacing the majority of the upper lateral of the sewer for my home. The upstairs bathroom was modernized by a previous owner with ABS lines that tie into a cast iron stack. That cast iron stack, and everything downstream of it up to the cleanout will be replaced (that is the section relevant to this construction permit, the section from the cleanout to where the repairs will be tied into the old cast iron relates to the sewer permit). This will involve removing the concrete pavers using a concrete saw, and then digging down by hand approximately a foot to reach the old cast iron, removing it. adding a bed of gravel, and then installing the new schedule 40 ABS piping& fittings. There are three main drainage points which are shown on the engineering drawing, a drain for the downstairs toilet, the main stack, and a drain for the upstairs kitchen sink/downstairs laundry room sink. I will schedule an inspection before starting work, to show an inspector the current sewer line layout and discuss my proposed fixes to ensure it will all meet local codes before starting any work. There is a PGE gas line near the sewer line, so I will call them first to identify where the line is to ensure it doesn't get disturbed during the work.

Metal doors are being upgraded to fiberglass doors with improved insulation properties. The current shearing and sheathing of the house and garage will be upgraded to the ZIP System 1/2” OSB with an approved and premanufactured Water-Resistive Barrier that meets all CRC and IBC requirements for Vapor and water movement. The current header will be used for both the front entry door and the back French door. Currently there are construction stairs inside the garage that will be replaced with an outside staircase-deck on both the west and east side of the garage. The plan is to build both decks free standing (no ledger board to the garage). I would like to defer obtaining permits for the decks as I need to complete siding, trim, windows, and doors so that I can complete scheduled termite fumigation on the house and garage.
